question: For three events $E$, $F$ and $G$ such that the required conditional probabilities are defined, use the definition of conditional probability to establish that $P(E\cap F\cap G)=P(E)P(F|E)P(G|E\cap F)$, and hence evaluate $P(E\cap F\cap G)$ when $P(E)=\frac{2}{3}$, $P(F|E)=\frac{3}{5}$ and $P(G|E\cap F)=\frac{1}{4}$.
explanation:
Formation of the Multiplication Relation
By the definition of conditional probability, provided $P(E\cap F)\ne0$,
$$P(G|E\cap F)=\frac{P(E\cap F\cap G)}{P(E\cap F)}.$$
Therefore,
$$P(E\cap F\cap G)=P(E\cap F)P(G|E\cap F).$$

Again, provided $P(E)\ne0$,
$$P(F|E)=\frac{P(E\cap F)}{P(E)},$$
so that
$$P(E\cap F)=P(E)P(F|E).$$
Substituting this result in the earlier expression gives
$$P(E\cap F\cap G)=P(E)P(F|E)P(G|E\cap F).$$
This is the multiplication theorem for the three events in the required form.

Evaluation
Using the given probabilities,
$$P(E\cap F\cap G)=\frac{2}{3}\times\frac{3}{5}\times\frac{1}{4}.$$
Therefore,
$$P(E\cap F\cap G)=\frac{6}{60}=\frac{1}{10}.$$

Final Result
Hence, $P(E\cap F\cap G)=P(E)P(F|E)P(G|E\cap F)$ and for the given data the required probability is $\frac{1}{10}$.
